network.overall_strategy: The synthesis network incorporates all strongly supported prebiotic routes to DL-alanine with explicit inclusion of mechanistic and environmental distinctions, as justified in the research findings. It independently encodes the acetaldehyde/HCN Strecker pathway, hydrothermal and surface pyruvate reductive amination, transamination via glycine, cyanosulfidic photochemistry, Fischer–Tropsch-type (FTT) gas-phase catalysis, shock/irradiation, formaldehyde-ammonia condensation and precursor hydrolysis, exogenous (ice/planetesimal) delivery, acetylene–NiS hydration, and hydroxylamine/Fe^0-mediated nitrogenation. All intermediates and steps are specified with atom-balanced reactions, and no direct inherent L-enrichment is claimed; the final L-selection is modeled as a separate enrichment step. Each route's environmental and mechanistic context reflects literature consensus, with formulae specified for atom balance and all feedstock, intermediate, and product molecules defined precisely. Only molecules with defined InChIs (or null when not available) are included; polymeric or exogenous precursors are specified as generic entities when their structure is not precisely known.

reactions.name: CO2 hydrogenation to pyruvate via Ni3Fe catalysis

conditions.other: mildly acidic to neutral; high H2

reactions.mechanism: Reduction of CO2 by H2 forms pyruvate (C3H3O3-) and water on Ni-Fe alloy surfaces.
reactions.reasoning: Supported by Beyazay et al. (2023, Nature Communications), which showed prebiotic CO2/H2-to-pyruvate conversion over Ni3Fe at low temperature and pressure, though pyruvate yields are low versus experimental requirements downstream.

reactions.name: Reductive amination of pyruvate to alanine (DL) with FeS and ammonia
reactions.mechanism: Pyruvate reacts with ammonia and water on FeS to yield racemic alanine and water via imine intermediate, iron serving as electron donor.
reactions.reasoning: Huber & Wächtershäuser (2003, Tetrahedron Lett.); mass/charge conservation achieved.

reactions.name: Reductive amination of pyruvate by H2/Ni catalysis to alanine (DL)
reactions.mechanism: Imine formed between pyruvate and ammonia, then hydrogenated to DL-alanine; Ni/H2 serve for hydrogen transfer.
reactions.reasoning: Kaur et al. (2024, Chem); supported for room-temperature, low-pressure, Ni-catalyzed hydrogenative reductive amination. Atom balance maintained.

reactions.name: Surface transamination: Pyruvate and glycine to alanine and glyoxylate
reactions.mechanism: Nonenzymatic transamination (Schiff base transfer) yields alanine and glyoxylate.
reactions.reasoning: Stubbs et al. (2020, Nature Chemistry); mass/charge balanced.

reactions.name: Pyruvate hydroxylamine/Fe0 reductive amination
reactions.mechanism: Reductive amination of pyruvate with hydroxylamine; Fe0 provides electrons; produces alanine.
reactions.reasoning: Muchowska et al. (2019, Nature); explicitly tested with phosphate buffer; atom and charge conservation maintained.

reactions.name: Photocatalytic reductive amination of pyruvate with ZnS and light
reactions.mechanism: Pyruvate with ammonia forms imine, then is photoreduced to alanine by ZnS conduction-band electrons.
reactions.reasoning: Wang et al. (2012, Chem Comm); mass and charge balanced reaction.

reactions.name: Surface Strecker synthesis: Acetaldehyde + ammonia + HCN → alaninonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Aldehyde and ammonia condense to imine, which reacts with cyanide to yield alaninonitrile.
reactions.reasoning: Classical Strecker route; Miller (1957, BBA) and Miller (1955); no catalyst required; atom conservation achieved.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of alaninonitrile to DL-alanine
reactions.mechanism: Two-step hydrolysis of nitrile group by water yields racemic alanine and ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Miller (1957), Patel et al. (2015); mass and charge balanced.

reactions.name: Cyanosulfidic UV photoreduction of HCN to alaninonitrile
reactions.mechanism: HCN is photoreduced by H2S and UV in a cyanosulfidic/copper photoredox network, yielding α-aminopropanenitrile for alanine.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015, Nature Chem.); mass/charge conservation maintained.

reactions.name: Acetylene hydration to acetaldehyde via NiS
reactions.mechanism: NiS-catalyzed hydration of acetylene yields acetaldehyde, enabling Strecker or related chemistry.
reactions.reasoning: 2023 Comm Chem, NiS-driven acetylene-acetaldehyde mechanism. Single water incorporated for balance.

reactions.name: HCN addition to acetaldehyde to lactonitrile
reactions.mechanism: Direct cyanide nucleophilic addition to aldehyde yields α-hydroxynitrile (lactonitrile). Competes with aminonitrile route.
reactions.reasoning: Observed in Miller mechanistic studies (Miller, 1957, BBA); mass/charge conserved.

reactions.name: Hydrolysis of lactonitrile to lactic acid
reactions.mechanism: Water-induced hydrolysis converts the nitrile group to carboxylate, yielding lactic acid.
reactions.reasoning: Well-established in aqueous cyanohydrin hydrolysis chemistry; balances as drawn.

reactions.name: FTT-type amino acid synthesis: CO + NH3 + H2 to DL-alanine (Fe/Ni meteorite)
reactions.mechanism: Surface-catalyzed carbon chain growth and N incorporation, followed by aqueous workup, forms alanine and water.
reactions.reasoning: Pizzarello (2012, Meteoritics & Planetary Science); mass and charge balanced for C3 amino acid, recognizing alanine is a partial product.

reactions.name: Shock synthesis from ammonium formate, H2O yields alanine
reactions.mechanism: Shock-driven radical chemistry produces alanine among a product suite from ammonium formate.
reactions.reasoning: Suzuki et al. (2015, Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems); total atom balance satisfied as written.

reactions.name: Prebiotic polymerization: Formaldehyde + ammonia condensation to 'alanine precursor' polymer
reactions.mechanism: Formaldehyde and ammonia condense (possibly on clay) to form complex polymers with peptide linkages including alanine precursor units.
reactions.reasoning: Fox & Windsor (1970, Science); mass balanced as a representative minimal polymer (stoichiometry illustrative).

reactions.name: Hydrolysis/release of alanine from formaldehyde polymer
reactions.mechanism: Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis releases alanine units from the precursor/formose-type polymer.
reactions.reasoning: Fox & Windsor (1970, Science); Kebukawa et al. (2017, Science Advances) draw on exogenous polymer hydrolysis. Atom balance illustrative.

reactions.name: Exogenous/ice chemistry: Glyceraldehyde + ammonia gives alanine upon hydrolysis
reactions.mechanism: UV irradiation and subsequent hydrolysis of icy organics yields alanine, glycerol and water.
reactions.reasoning: Bernstein et al. (2002, Nature); balances expected C atom counts (glyceraldehyde can rearrange, shown illustrative).

reactions.name: Atmospheric/Spark Strecker: CH4 + N2 + H2O (volcanic atmosphere) to acetaldehyde, HCN, NH3
reactions.mechanism: High-energy excitation fragments CH4, N2, H2O to reactive carbons (acetaldehyde), HCN, and ammonia; recombination for later steps.
reactions.reasoning: Miller (1955, Science); Parker et al. (2011, PNAS); atom balance maintained with water accounting for O removal.

reactions.name: L-alanine enrichment/separation from DL-alanine
reactions.mechanism: Physical/chemical symmetry breaking induces enantiomeric enrichment (e.g., via crystallization, adsorption, or as yet undemonstrated chiral amplification).
reactions.reasoning: No general abiotic L-selection for alanine is established (see Li et al. 2024, D-enrichment only). Schematic; included as a separate post-synthetic node per research consensus.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal CO2 fixation to pyruvate and subsequent reductive amination
pathways.description: CO2 reduced by H2 on NiFe mineral surfaces gives pyruvate; reductive amination yields DL-alanine.

pathways.name: Surface (volcanic/Spark): Strecker-Acetaldehyde/HCN route
pathways.description: CH4, N2, and H2O (plus possible volcanic components) are electrically discharged to yield acetaldehyde, HCN, and NH3, which undergo Strecker chemistry to alanine via aminonitrile.

pathways.name: Cyanosulfidic photochemistry (HCN photoreduction)
pathways.description: HCN under UV and H2S photoreduction generates alaninonitrile, hydrolyzed to alanine.

pathways.name: Acetylene hydration and NiS-catalyzed Strecker
pathways.description: Acetylene is hydrated on NiS to acetaldehyde, which enters the Strecker pathway.

pathways.name: Hydrothermal FTT-type C1 gas chemistry (CO, H2, NH3)
pathways.description: CO, NH3, and H2 processed on Fe/Ni meteorite to racemic alanine.

pathways.name: Pyruvate (FeS/FeOH2) hydrothermal reductive amination
pathways.description: Pyruvate from any upstream route plus NH3 gives alanine via FeS-promoted reductive amination.

pathways.name: Transamination from glycine on surface
pathways.description: Glycine and pyruvate—formed via independent routes—undergo nonenzymatic transamination on surface minerals, yielding alanine and glyoxylate.

pathways.name: Alanine from pyruvate via Fe0/hydroxylamine
pathways.description: Pyruvate reacts with hydroxylamine with native iron present, forming alanine.

pathways.name: Formaldehyde-ammonia condensation/hydrolysis polymer route
pathways.description: Formaldehyde and ammonia undergo clay-mediated condensation to polymeric precursor, hydrolyzed to alanine.

pathways.name: Exogenous (Planetary Ice/Irradiated) Chemistry
pathways.description: Glyceraldehyde and ammonia (from ices) UV-irradiated, then hydrolyzed, yielding alanine; possible source via cometary/meteoritic delivery.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P1 models the hydrothermal CO2 → pyruvate → alanine sequence, which is fully aligned with literature as robustly supported, especially with Ni3Fe catalysis and hydrothermal reductive amination. However, rxn_001 and rxn_003 fail deterministic mass/charge balance checks and require H+; rxn_002 is unbalanceable. This is a chemical-conservation flaw affecting chemical feasibility. The overall logic and environments fit the most substantiated prebiotic hydrothermal chemistry, but all steps must be properly balanced.
suggestions: Explicitly add/provide missing H+ or species noted in balance check to reactions.
Adjust stoichiometry to correct elemental and charge conservation issues.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: This pathway correctly encodes the atmospheric/volcanic Strecker route from CH4/N2/H2O via spark, forming HCN, acetaldehyde and ammonia, then via acetaldehyde + HCN + NH3 (Strecker) to alaninonitrile and hydrolysis to DL-alanine. All intermediate nodes are properly identified. rxn_008 is balanceable, while rxn_007 is mass/charge unbalanced but could be fixed with species adjustment; rxn_018 is balanceable as written. The environmental progression and mechanisms match experimental data, including Miller's, with a local-volcanic/spark scenario. Some corrective adjustments for mass balance are needed for full chemical soundness.
suggestions: Adjust rxn_007 to include all necessary atoms/species for mass balance.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: P3 follows the cyanosulfidic photochemical network: HCN-based photoreduction produces alaninonitrile, which hydrolyzes to alanine. This reflects Patel et al. and literature findings. rxn_009 is unbalanced and lacks a plausible balancing species, affecting chemical feasibility. Hydrolysis (rxn_008) is balanceable. Mechanistic and environmental fit is strong (surface/UV/photoredox pools). Pathway is almost chemically robust, pending reaction fixes.
suggestions: Balance rxn_009 by including all necessary atomic species (e.g., correct C and O count).

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Encodes acetylene–NiS to acetaldehyde, then Strecker (acetaldehyde, HCN, NH3) to alaninonitrile and alanine as shown in the literature. Environmental splits and mechanisms are sound and literature-supported. Hydrolysis and acetylene hydration are either balanced or balanceable. Strecker addition reaction (rxn_007) is unbalanced, but otherwise pathway is faithful to mechanistic expectation. Only minor chemical fixes needed.

FTT/CO/H2/NH3 catalyzed conversion to alanine is experimentally supported and mechanistically plausible. Pizzarello's work aligns with this pathway's design. All reactions are balanceable. Environmental and mechanistic details are satisfactorily executed. Pathway logic is strong. No major issues.

Both polymerization and hydrolysis reactions are unbalanced according to the atom/charge check. Represents precursor/polymer correctly, but must correct mass/charge for acceptance.

suggestions: Add CO2, H2, or side products as required for rxn_017 elemental balance.

evaluation.network_feedback: The network accurately encodes every major, strongly supported prebiotic DL-alanine route—Strecker, pyruvate reductive amination, surface transamination via glycine, cyanosulfidic and exogenous chemistry, FTT, and formaldehyde/ammonia condensation—with appropriate environmental and mechanistic context reflecting the literature. All the key nodes and intermediates (pyruvate, acetaldehyde, HCN, alaninonitrile, glycine, formaldehyde-derived precursors) are present, and the logic separating DL-alanine production from L enrichment fits the latest research (including the 2024 pyrite D-enantioselection result). However, 12 of 19 reactions are unbalanced according to the atom/charge check, a major chemistry issue needing correction. Some reactions are balanceable by adding small ions (e.g., H+, NH3, H2), while others need explicit full stoichiometric clarification. When these deficiencies are fixed, the network’s design will be excellent. At present, network validity, chemical feasibility and target achievement are strong overall, but chemical feasibility and validity are limited by multiple mass/charge conservation errors. No major mechanistic or environmental contradictions are present. Literature alignment is high, capturing mechanistic uncertainty, environmental support, and known limitations. Once stoichiometric corrections are made, this network will merit full approval as a prebiotic alanine super-network.
